story: Copying listing-template pieces seen earlier in the passage: the OO of GOOGLE and day names completing ranges like Mon-Sat or Fri & Sat (the am/Mon completions after clock times belong elsewhere).
Predicting 'the' or 'a' starting a noun phrase right after a linking verb or 'and' (this pier is the..., and a...), not after prepositions.
Late in the window, continuing web-address and map boilerplate in listings: the uk of .co.uk, the MAP of GOOGLE MAP, the '/' after uk, and the ' ;' separator after a closing bracket.
Predicting the period that ends a descriptive sentence at its final word in flowing prose (whenever the sun shines., best bars and nightlife.).
Closing the parenthesis right after the opening-hours, dates or prices that end a listing's practical details (…10am-5.30pm Mar-Sep), not after prose.
Predicting 'the' or 'a' immediately after the prepositions 'of', 'at' or 'from' in ordinary prose.
Late in the window, continuing a word the tokenizer split mid-way (Sax->ons, Belg->rav, Panc->ras), producing a no-space lowercase word fragment.
Predicting the newline that ends a map-index line after its grid reference digit (47Duke of WellingtonD4, 40Monmouth Coffee CompanyF3).
Closing a paired delimiter - parenthesis, bold '**', italic '_' or quote - to match the opener that appeared earlier, whatever word precedes it.
Early-layer completion of tight two-word habits from the immediately preceding word: Named after, Billed as, Kicking off, Begun in, your fill of, Mountains of, slabs of.
Early in the window, continuing a word the tokenizer split mid-way (Cam->bridge, amb->ience, bur->les), producing a no-space lowercase word fragment.
